extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry / specialists in Inter-universal Teichmüller (IUT) theory
extracted.subtask_description: Develop and analyze functorial group-theoretic algorithms to reconstruct tempered fundamental-group data, decomposition groups, and to perform Hodge–Arakelov-theoretic evaluation of étale theta functions at torsion/evaluation points; treat conjugacy indeterminacies and synchronization issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstruct diagram of tempered groups from Πtp_X
rubrics_metrics.description: The diagram of open injections of topological groups arising from the tempered fundamental groups Πtp X_v, Πtp Y_v, Πtp ¨Y_v (with cartesian squares and natural inclusions) may be reconstructed via a functorial group-theoretic algorithm from the topological group Πtp_X_v (i.e., from Πtp_X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This uses the theory of [EtTh], §2 and results such as [EtTh], Proposition 2.4 and [SemiAnbd], Example 3.10; the reconstruction treats the open subgroups determined by the various tempered coverings and respects the cartesian squares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special-fiber dual-graph vertex bijection
rubrics_metrics.description: For models of ¨Y_v arising from a stable model of X_v, the special fiber consists of a chain of projective lines; the set of irreducible components is a Z-torsor and the natural maps on dual graphs determined by the coverings induce bijections on vertices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequence of total ramification at cusps and the exact sequence of Galois groups; used to relate dual graphs of various coverings and to choose connected components for group-theoretic reconstruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of canonical connected subgraphs Γ^(4)_X and Γ•_X
rubrics_metrics.description: There are unique connected subgraphs Γ^(4)_X (a tree stabilized by inversion ι_X containing every vertex) and Γ•_X (stabilized by ι_X containing exactly one vertex and no edges) obtained by eliminating appropriate edges; corresponding stabilized connected components exist for covering dual graphs and map bijectively/isomorphically to Γ^(4)_X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These subgraphs are used to define decomposition groups and to fix a single connected component (basepoint) for subsequent constructions; divisibility at edges of the theta-pole divisor shows the maps are isomorphisms when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstruct decomposition-group chain from Π_v
rubrics_metrics.description: The chain of decomposition groups Πv• ⊆ Πv^(4) ⊆ Πv determined by Γ•_X ⊆ Γ^(4)_X ⊆ ΓX (and an involution ι) may be reconstructed, up to Πv-conjugacy, via a functorial group-theoretic algorithm from the topological group Πv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses dual-graph reconstruction algorithms (e.g., [SemiAnbd], Corollary 3.11 or [AbsTopI], Theorem 2.14) and the commensurably terminal property to pin down subgroups up to conjugacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct θ(Π_v) and select canonical ι-invariant orbits
rubrics_metrics.description: Functorial group-theoretic algorithms produce θ(Π_v) ⊆ ∞θ(Π_v) and, imposing invariance under the involution ι, determine a specific μ_{2l}- (respectively μ-) orbit θ_ι(Π_v) (respectively ∞θ_ι(Π_v)) inside the unique {(l·Z)×μ_{2l}}- (resp. {(l·Z)×μ}-) orbit contained in θ(Π_v) (resp. ∞θ(Π_v)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This selection depends on the invariance condition with respect to ι and references [EtTh], Proposition 1.4 and related results; orbits are determined functorially from Πv.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjugacy indeterminacy is inner on Π_v^(4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Πv^(4) ⊆ Πv is commensurably terminal, any Πv-conjugacy indeterminacy of this subgroup induces an indeterminacy on any chosen Πv-conjugate that is only by inner automorphisms of that conjugate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hence once a representative is fixed, remaining ambiguity is inner-conjugation ambiguity; used to control stabilization by representatives of involutions ι.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambient diagrams Δ_v → Δ±_v → Δcor_v recoverable from Π_v
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural diagrams of outer inclusions Δ_v → Δ±_v → Δcor_v and their profinite completions embed as normal open subgroups with prescribed indices (Δ± of index 2l, etc.) and the groups Π±_v and Πcor_v may be reconstructed group-theoretically from Πv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: [EtTh], Proposition 2.2 and Proposition 2.4; these diagrams provide ambient containers for local conjugacy classes and torsor structures used throughout the theta-evaluation algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstruct cuspidal inertia groups algorithmically
rubrics_metrics.description: Cuspidal inertia groups of a larger group Π⊇ can be reconstructed group-theoretically from Π⊇ via the algorithms of [AbsTopI] (Lemma 4.5, Proposition 4.10); cuspidal inertia groups of a subgroup Π⊆ are obtained as intersections with Π⊆ of those of Π⊇, and commensurators/normalizers yield Π⊇-conjugates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a method to identify inertia subgroups inside various ambient groups and to transfer information between Π⊇ and Π⊆ when inclusions correspond to totally ramified coverings.

rubrics_metrics.name: ±-label classes of cusps and torsor structure LabCusp±
rubrics_metrics.description: Define LabCusp±(Π⊆) as the set of ±-label classes of cusps (Π⊆-conjugacy classes of cuspidal inertia subgroups whose commensurators in Π⊇ determine a single Π⊇-conjugacy class). LabCusp±(Πv) admits an F_l^×-action, a distinguished zero element †η0_v and a ±-canonical element †η±_v (well-defined up to ±1) constructible from †D_v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These labels correspond to vertices of Γ^(4)_X and are used to index theta-values and evaluation points; identification is functorial in the relevant group data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence criteria for inclusions/conjugation (Cor. 2.4 (i))
rubrics_metrics.description: For conjugates γ, γ' in Δ±_v, the following are equivalent: (a) γ' ∈ Δ±_v(cid:5); (b) I_{γ·γ'}^t ⊆ Π^v(cid:5)_{γ}; (c) I_{γ·γ'}^t ⊆ (Π±_v(cid:5))_{γ}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This logical equivalence provides a group-theoretic test to detect when a conjugate lands in the relevant finite-index subgroup; used in identifying translates of cusps and their containment relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-torsion translates determine decomposition groups
rubrics_metrics.description: An inclusion I^δ_t ⊆ Π^δ_v(cid:5) arising from a μ-translate determines (a) a decomposition group D^δ_t = N_{Π^δ_v}(I^δ_t) inside Π^δ_v¨(cid:5), (b) a decomposition group D^δ_{t,μ-} in Π^δ_v¨(cid:4) corresponding to the torsion point μ-, and (c) a decomposition group D^δ_v¨(cid:5) (image of an evaluation section) corresponding to the μ--translate of the cusp; these are well-defined up to the indicated conjugacies and compatible with conjugation by Δ±_v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructed via algorithms of [SemiAnbd], Theorem 6.8 (group-theoreticity of decomposition groups of torsion points) and Corollary 3.11 (dual semi-graphs).

rubrics_metrics.name: F_l^±-symmetry compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: When (cid:4)=•_t, the constructions of decomposition groups and translates are compatible with conjugation by arbitrary elements of Πcor_v and in particular respect the F_l^±-symmetry realized by natural outer isomorphisms Πcor_v/Π±_v ∼→ F_l^±.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This symmetry constrains μ_{2l}-indeterminacies and ensures that certain orbits are stable under the larger commensurator action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow replacement of inertia by maximal pro-l' subgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: It is permissible (and often simplifying) to replace an inertia subgroup I_t by its maximal pro-l' subgroup for any l' ∈ Primes \ {p_v}; closed subgroups of such maximal pro-l' subgroups are either open or trivial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This simplifies intersections with other closed subgroups and is justified via [IUTchI], Proposition 2.4 and subsequent remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction isomorphism for (l·ΔΘ) subquotients
rubrics_metrics.description: The inclusion Π_v¨(cid:4) → Π_v induces an isomorphism (l·ΔΘ)(Π_v¨(cid:4)) ∼→ (l·ΔΘ)(Π_v); quotients Π_v (3) G_v(Π_v) and Π_v¨(cid:4) (3) G_v(Π_v¨(cid:4)) are constructible by functorial group-theoretic algorithms from Π_v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies the relevant subquotients used to define the cohomology groups where theta-values live and ensures computations may be carried out on subgraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction of étale theta-functions yields μ_{2l}, μ-orbits depending only on label
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction of the ι_γ-invariant sets θ_ι(Π^γ_v) to Π^γ_v¨(cid:4) yields μ_{2l}- and μ-orbits θ_{|t|}(Π^γ_v¨(cid:4)), ∞θ_{|t|}(Π^γ_v¨(cid:4)) in lim_H^1(...,(l·ΔΘ)(...)) which, upon further restriction to decomposition groups D^δ_{t,μ-}, produce orbits θ_t and ∞θ_t that depend only on the label |t| ∈ |F_l| determined by t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus theta-values attached to evaluation points are well-defined up to the indicated multiplicative indeterminacies and depend only on the cusp label rather than conjugacy representative; see references to Kummer map and [IUTchI], Example 4.4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial group-theoretic evaluation algorithm
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting from arbitrary Δ±_v-conjugate Π^γ_v¨(cid:4) and varying t over LabCusp±(Π^γ_v), one obtains a functorial group-theoretic algorithm producing the collections {θ_{|t|}(Π^γ_v¨(cid:4))}_{|t|∈|F_l|} and {∞θ_{|t|}(Π^γ_v¨(cid:4))}_{|t|∈|F_l|} which are functorial in Π_v and compatible with independent conjugacy actions of Δ±_v and the indicated Π-sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives an algorithmic prescription for producing all relevant theta-orbits from the topological group data, compatible with conjugation actions described in Corollary 2.4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theta-values under cyclotomic rigidity and functional equations
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the standard cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism (∗_{bs-Gal}) and the Kummer map, for j ∈ |F_l| the set θ_j(Π_v¨(cid:4)) is precisely the μ_{2l}-orbit of q_v^{j^2/2}; reciprocals of the l-th powers of these theta-values satisfy that ratios ¨Θ(c)/¨Θ(c') are roots of unity when c' arises from c by an automorphism inducing a unit quotient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These arithmetic properties are computed from the theta-series functional equations ([EtTh], Proposition 1.4) and are central to identifying the numerical values attached to the abstract cohomology classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence / lack of synchronization of μ_{2l}-indeterminacies
rubrics_metrics.description: The various μ_{2l}-multiple indeterminacies occurring for different labels j ∈ |F_l| in the μ_{2l}-orbit θ_j(Π_v¨(cid:4)) are independent (not synchronized); each arises from the action of (Δ±_{v•t}/Δ_v¨•t)^δ on decomposition groups and hence from Δcor_v-outer actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a key structural obstruction: indeterminacies for distinct labels cannot be collapsed to a single global indeterminacy, which impacts Kummer-theoretic arguments and the need for conjugate synchronization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global ambient bridge Δ(cid:6)± and limits of globalization
rubrics_metrics.description: The global object Δ(cid:6)± ∼= Δ±_v is independent of v and can serve as an ambient container (a 'global bridge') for conjugates of local objects like It and Δ_v¨(cid:4), but the local groups Π_v¨(cid:4) do not admit globalizations across multiple v’s; conjugacy indeterminacies propagate: G_v-conjugacy indeterminacy ⇒ Δ±_v-conjugacy indeterminacy ⇒ independent G_v-conjugacy indeterminacies for GK, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes how local-to-global passage works in the theory and explains why many indeterminacies must be treated as independent when moving among primes v; non-splitting of natural surjections enforces independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: M×TM-subsets and splittings on subgraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotients G_v(Π_v¨(cid:4)) determine subsets M×TM·θ_ι(Π^γ_v¨(cid:4)) ⊆ lim H^1(...); for zero-labeled evaluation points t=0, θ_t equals the μ_{2l}- (resp. μ-) orbit of the identity cohomology class, and restriction to decomposition groups yields splittings of M×TM-modules compatible with splittings of Corollary 1.12.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the module-theoretic framework (M×TM and torsion submodules) required to obtain canonical splittings at special evaluation points and to control torsion phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjugate synchronization (single-basepoint requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The theta-evaluation algorithm must be performed relative to a single basepoint (a single connected subgraph Γ^(4)_X copy) — i.e., all theta-values for various labels |t| ∈ F_l should be computed relative to the same copy of the Galois group G_v(Π_v¨(cid:4)) and the same cyclotome (module of N-th roots of unity); this phenomenon is termed conjugate synchronization and is necessary for performing Kummer theory on the collection of theta values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conjugate synchronization is required to treat the collection of theta values as a unified entity for simultaneous extraction of N-th roots and to ensure compatibility with Kummer-theoretic Galois evaluation; it underlies later Gaussian Frobenioid constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility of conjugate synchronization with label synchronization and F_l^±-symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: The single basepoint underlying conjugate synchronization is compatible with the single basepoint that underlies label synchronization in [IUTchI], so conjugate synchronization is compatible with the F_l^±-symmetry described in [IUTchI], Proposition 6.8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This compatibility ensures the various synchronizations (basepoints for conjugacy and for labeling) can be chosen consistently, a fact used in proving Corollary 2.4 (iii) and later constructions.
